sourceSpan.excerpt: Lack of an answer to the problem of evil. Look, as long as God can bring more good from any evil that exists, God and evil are not logically incompatible. Dan has the burden of proving God could never have a good reason to allow evil to exist, because he's the one making the argument. We can think of good reasons. God allows moral evil so we can have free will and be able to truly choose the good. That's just one. In fact, the atheist J.L. Mackey says, the problem of evil does not show that the central doctrines of theism are logically inconsistent with one another. Dan's argument also cuts against his own position. Those children in the hospital, we have a moral duty to care for them. Even if by euthanizing them, we could save many more lives. But this shows we have universal moral duties, whose source must be the perfect standard of goodness itself. Thus, Stan's arguments against God now becomes an argument for God.

sourceSpan.excerpt: Trent says that the question of God is not a scientific question. That's wrong. The question of the existence of God is a scientific question. If it's not, then it's not a question we can even debate. A universe with a God in it would look totally different than a universe without a God in it. And obviously, you believers think that God answers prayer. That should be a difference. If there were no God, then you would see no prayers answered. And yet, you believers think that prayers are answered. The universe is physically different because of the existence of this God. Don't you think so? Don't you think that that God has effects in the real world? The existence of God is a scientific question and can be tested scientifically. And when we do look at prayer, we see that the success rate of prayer is no better than a random chance. Except for things like feeling better and, you know, having better mind control and meditation in that, let's say.
